A: <u>For the purposes of this section and of subdivision B 4 f of § 51.1-142.2, a written statement, notice, or certification required of the Board is given on the date the Board mails it to the person to whom it is required to be given or transmits it electronically to an address that person has provided to the Board for that purpose, except that an electronic transmission completed after 5:00 p.m. is given on the following day. For the purposes of this section and of subdivision B 4 f of § 51.1-142.2, where the Board mails a written statement, notice, or certification, every period within which a person may or must act that runs from the giving of that statement, notice, or certification is extended by three days. ***For the purposes of this section and of subdivision B 4 f of § 51.1-142.2, where a period begins or ends upon, or is measured from, the Board's acting, or last acting, upon a request, or where a date is fixed by reference to the month in which the Board acts, or last acts, upon a request, the Board is deemed to act upon that request, and to last act upon it, on the date on which the Board first acts upon it. Except for the purposes of the duty of the Board under subsection M to act upon an application no later than 15 days after it acts upon the request, nothing in the preceding sentence determines the date by which the Board is required to act upon a request, to make a determination, or to give a notice or a decision, or whether the Board has performed such a duty within a period required by this section.***</u>
DEF: <u>"Final qualifying retirement date" means the date that is 12 months after the member's earliest qualifying retirement date, except that the Board shall approve a later date where the Board's own processing requirements, or any other cause not attributable to the member, make the member's retirement on or before the date that would otherwise apply under this definition impracticable. A later date approved under this definition shall be the first day of a month and shall be not more than three months after the date determined under the first sentence of this definition. The Board shall approve a later date on its own initiative or upon the written request of the member, which the member may file at any time before the date that would otherwise apply under this definition or before any later date approved under this definition; the Board shall act upon such a request, and shall give the member written notice of its determination and of the reasons for it, no later than 30 days after the request is filed; and the member may seek review of the determination under subsection M. The Board shall determine the member's earliest qualifying retirement date and final qualifying retirement date, and shall state both of them and the reasons for any later date approved under this definition, in writing to the member no later than 15 days after the Board credits to the member the service credit purchased under the member's election, and shall give the member written notice of any later date approved after that statement no later than 15 days after the approval. Where the member's final qualifying retirement date as extended under subdivision D 1 or as tolled under subsection M is not the first day of a month, the member's final qualifying retirement date is the first day of the next month. In no event shall a member's final qualifying retirement date, as extended under subdivision D 1 or as tolled under subsection M, be later than 12 months after the date that applies under the first sentence of this definition or, where a later date has been approved under this definition, after that later date, except that this sentence does not apply to an extension under subdivision D 1 by reason of a statement or notice given later than the time required by this definition, and the aggregate of all extensions so excluded shall not exceed 12 months. Where the running of a period has been tolled under subsection M and the member is prevented by the preceding sentence from retiring in a qualifying retirement after that tolling ends, the member's final qualifying retirement date is, notwithstanding the preceding sentence, the first day of the second month following the month in which the Board last acts upon a request the filing of which tolled that period, and in no event later than 12 months after the latest date the preceding sentence permits. Notwithstanding the two preceding sentences, where the date that would otherwise apply under this definition is earlier than the first day of the second month following the month in which the Board gives the statement required by this definition, the member's final qualifying retirement date is that first day. Where the Board does not act upon a request the filing of which tolled the running of the member's final qualifying retirement date under subsection M within the period ~~this definition allows~~ **allowed by this section** for acting upon it, and the date that would otherwise apply under this definition is earlier than the first day of the second month following the month in which that period expired, the member's final qualifying retirement date is, notwithstanding any other provision of this definition, that first day. Where the Board's action upon a request determines a member's final qualifying retirement date under this definition, the Board shall state that date in its decision upon the request, and where the Board does not do so it shall give the member written notice of that date no later than 15 days after ~~it acts upon~~ ***it gives its decision upon*** the request***, except that where the request is denied otherwise than by a decision of the Board upon it, or where the period allowed by this section for acting upon the request expires without the Board's acting upon it, it shall give that notice no later than 15 days after the date on which the Board acts upon the request***. Where the date that would otherwise apply under this definition is earlier than the first day of the second month following the month in which the Board gives a decision or notice required by the preceding sentence, the member's final qualifying retirement date is, notwithstanding any other provision of this definition, that first day.</u>
D1: <u>**D. 1.** The Board shall not accept an election until the Board has, in writing, certified to the member and reserved the certified subsidy for that election under this subsection. The Board shall determine the certified subsidy for an election no later than 30 days after the member's application is completed. The Board shall give the certification required by this subsection no later than 15 days after the Director of the Department of Planning and Budget or his designee acts upon the Board's request under subdivision 3. The Board's certification shall state the matters required by subdivision B 4 c of § 51.1-142.2, the filing date of the member's complete application, the amount of service credit to be purchased, the certified subsidy, the valuation date, the completion date by which the member must complete payment, the member's anticipated earliest qualifying retirement date and anticipated final qualifying retirement date, the member's unreduced retirement eligibility date determined with the service credit to be purchased as certified, the member's right to cancel the election under subdivision G 5 at any time before completing payment, and the member's obligations under subsections E, F, and G. The Board shall not accept an election until the member has filed with the Board a written acknowledgment of the member's obligations under subsections E, F, and G. The Board's certification shall also state that, where a member whose election the Board has accepted dies without having retired, the benefit payable on the member's death is determined under subdivision G 4 and under § 51.1-162 as on the death of a member in service and not under the provisions of subdivision C 1 of § 51.1-165 or of subsection F of § 51.1-165.01 that require benefits to be paid in accordance with § 51.1-163; that where the member dies while in service and subdivision C 2 of § 51.1-165 otherwise applies, that subdivision provides for the payment of benefits in accordance with § 51.1-163, except that where the contingent annuitant or annuitants under the option elected are the same person or persons who would receive a monthly benefit under subsection B of § 51.1-162 and that monthly benefit would be greater, that subdivision provides for the payment of benefits in accordance with that subsection, and that the Board shall pay the benefit that subdivision provides or the benefit determined under subdivision G 4, whichever is greater; that no option elected under subdivision A 2 or A 3 of § 51.1-165 limits that benefit; that subsection C of § 51.1-165.01 provides that any optional payment of the retirement allowance pursuant to § 51.1-165 is based upon the retirement allowance as reduced to reflect a lump-sum distribution elected under that section; but that the straight life option under subdivision A 1 of § 51.1-165 is an election to receive an increased retirement allowance in lieu of any death benefits and, where that election is not rendered null and void by subdivision C 1 of § 51.1-165, may leave no benefit payable on the member's death; that, to the extent required by § 401(a)(37) of the Internal Revenue Code, as amended or renumbered, and the regulations thereunder applicable to governmental plans, subsection B of § 51.1-162 provides a retirement allowance on the death of a member in service only where no benefit is payable under subsection C of that section and only to a surviving spouse, minor child, or parent whom the member has designated under subsection A of that section or who is entitled in the order of precedence that subsection B of that section states where the member has made no designation or the person designated has predeceased the member and no other designation has been made; that subsection C of § 51.1-162 provides a retirement allowance, where the member dies in service from a cause compensable under the Virginia Workers' Compensation Act (§ 65.2-100 et seq.), to the member's surviving spouse, minor children, or parents as that subsection provides; that where no benefit is payable under subsection B of § 51.1-162, subsection A of that section provides for the payment of the member's accumulated contributions, reduced by the amount of any retirement allowance previously received by the member under this chapter or the abolished system, to the person the member has designated or, where the member has made no designation or the person designated has predeceased the member and no other designation has been made, to a surviving relative in the order of precedence that section states; and that the Board advises the member to review the member's designation of beneficiary under subsection A of § 51.1-162, and the effect of that designation under subsection B of that section, before completing payment, that the member may make or change that designation under subsection A of that section at any time before the member's death, and that nothing in this subdivision requires the member to review the designation or affects any benefit by reason of the member's not having reviewed it. A failure to state in the Board's certification every matter this subdivision requires to be stated in it, other than a failure to state that the Board advises the member to review the member's designation of beneficiary, is a failure of the Board to state in a certification a matter this section requires to be stated in it for the purposes of subsection M; a person adversely affected by it may seek review under subsection M no later than 30 days after the date on which the certification is given to the member or, where that person is not the member, no later than 30 days after the date on which the notice required by subdivision G 4 is given to that person; the second sentence of subdivision M 2 does not apply to such a failure where the person adversely affected is the member; and the Board shall state every such failure, and every failure to state that the Board advises the member to review the member's designation of beneficiary, in the report required by subsection J. The member shall file the notice of retirement required by § 51.1-153, stating as the effective date of retirement a date on which the member will retire in a qualifying retirement, no later than 30 days after the date on which the Board gives the member the written statement of the member's earliest qualifying retirement date and final qualifying retirement date first required by the definition of "final qualifying retirement date" in subsection A. Nothing in this subdivision requires the member to file that notice any period before the effective date of retirement stated in it. A notice filed within the period allowed by this subdivision satisfies § 51.1-153 notwithstanding that it is filed after the effective date of retirement stated in it; and where such a notice is filed after that effective date, the member's retirement shall take effect on that date and the retirement allowance shall be payable retroactively to that date, subject to subsection E of § 51.1-153 and provided that the effective date stated is on or after the day following the member's last day of service. The Board shall state the period allowed by this subdivision in the written statement required by that definition. Where the Board gives that written statement, any notice of a later approved date required by that definition, or any notice of a date required by that definition ~~upon~~ **by reason of** the Board's action upon a request, later than the time required by that definition, the member's final qualifying retirement date is extended by the number of days by which the statement or notice is late, the member may state an effective date of retirement that is no earlier than the first day of the month following the month in which the Board gives the statement or notice, and the Board shall state every such delay in the report required by subsection J. **Where the Board gives any notice of a kind described in the preceding sentence after the expiration of the period allowed by this subdivision for filing the notice of retirement required by § 51.1-153, the member may file that notice of retirement, or a notice replacing a notice of retirement already filed by the member, no later than 30 days after the Board gives the notice; and a notice so filed is filed within the period allowed by this subdivision and supersedes any notice of retirement previously filed by the member, except that no notice may be filed under this sentence after the member has retired.** The Board shall state, in the written statement required by that definition**,** ~~and~~ in every notice of a later approved date required by that definition, **and in every notice of a date required by that definition by reason of the Board's action upon a request,** (i) that where the Board gives the statement or notice later than the time required by that definition the member's final qualifying retirement date is extended by the number of days by which the statement or notice is late, that the date so extended is subject to the limits stated in that definition, and that where the date so extended is not the first day of a month it is the first day of the next month; (ii) that the member may state as the effective date of retirement a date no earlier than the first day of the month following the month in which the Board gives the statement or notice, and that nothing in this subdivision prevents the member from stating an earlier effective date of retirement to which the member is otherwise entitled, subject to subsection E of § 51.1-153**;** ~~and~~ **(iii)** that where the Board mails the statement or notice, every period that runs from the giving of it is extended by three days**; and (iv) that where the Board gives a notice of a kind described in this sentence after the expiration of the period allowed by this subdivision for filing the notice of retirement required by § 51.1-153 and the member has not retired, the member may file that notice of retirement, or a notice replacing a notice of retirement already filed by the member, no later than 30 days after the Board gives that notice, and that a notice so filed is filed within the period allowed by this subdivision and supersedes any notice of retirement previously filed by the member**.</u>
G2: <u>2. If the member does not retire in a qualifying retirement, the Board shall, except as subdivision 4 provides, within 60 days after the earlier of (a) the member's final qualifying retirement date, if any, and (b) the date on which the member retires in a retirement that is not a qualifying retirement, (i) reduce the service credit credited to the member under the election to the largest number of whole months of service credit that the member's payments would have purchased at the standard cost determined as of the date the Board accepted the election, (ii) refund to the member, and to any state agency from whose appropriation an amount was paid on the member's behalf, in proportion to the amounts each paid, the amount by which the amounts paid exceed the cost, at that standard cost, of the service credit credited under clause (i), and (iii) release the reservation. The Board shall give the member written notice of the determination, of the service credit retained, and of the reasons for the determination, no less than 30 days, and in no case less than the period allowed to the member by subsection M within which to request reconsideration of the determination, before the determination takes effect, and a determination that takes effect in contravention of this sentence takes effect instead on the first day on which it may take effect under this sentence; and the member may seek review of the determination under subsection M. The Board shall not pay any retirement allowance to a member whose election has not been settled under subdivision 1 or 4 until the Board has made the determination required by this subdivision, and the determination shall take effect before the first payment of any retirement allowance to the member; and the first payment of the retirement allowance shall include every amount that would have been payable to the member from the effective date of retirement had the determination been made before the effective date of retirement. Nothing in this subdivision prevents the payment of a retirement allowance to a member while an application of the member for a disability retirement allowance under this chapter is pending, and the determination required by this subdivision shall take effect notwithstanding that a retirement allowance has been paid to the member while such an application was pending. **For the purposes of this subdivision, an application of the member for a disability retirement allowance under this chapter is pending from the date on which the member files it until the date on which the Board grants or denies it.** No determination under this subdivision is required in respect of an election that has been cancelled under subdivision D 6 or under subdivision 5 of this subsection, in respect of an election under which the member has been credited with service credit under subdivision 3 or 5 of this subsection, or in respect of an election under which the reservation has been released under subdivision D 7 without any service credit having been credited to the member, and no retirement allowance shall be withheld by reason of this subdivision on account of any such election. For the purposes of this subdivision, "the determination date" means the date from which the 60-day period within which the Board must make the determination required by this subdivision runs, whether that period runs under the first sentence of this subdivision or under subdivision 4. The Board shall give the notice required by this subdivision no later than 60 days after the determination date, and shall state in the report required by subsection J every failure to give that notice within that period. A determination under this subdivision shall take effect no later than 60 days after the Board gives the notice required by this subdivision, and in no event later than 120 days after the determination date, except that where the Board gives that notice later than 60 days after the determination date, or has not given it within 60 days after the determination date, **or where the determination could not take effect within 120 days after the determination date consistently with the requirement of this subdivision that notice be given no less than 30 days, and in no case less than the period allowed to the member by subsection M within which to request reconsideration of the determination, before the determination takes effect,** the determination takes effect on the first day on which it may take effect under the sentence of this subdivision that requires notice to be given no less than 30 days before the determination takes effect, and in that case the limit of 120 days stated in this sentence does not apply. Where the member dies before the first payment of the retirement allowance, the Board shall pay the amount that would have been included in that payment under this subdivision to the person entitled to any benefit payable on the member's death or, if there is none, to the member's estate. The Board shall pay a refund required by this subdivision within 60 days after the determination takes effect, except that to the extent a refund may not be paid to the member without adverse federal tax consequence to the member, the Board shall apply that amount to the purchase of additional service credit for the member at the standard cost and shall notify the member in writing of the amount so applied.</u>
G4: > The Board shall not make a determination under subdivision 2, and shall not give the notice required by subdivision 2, while an application of the member for a disability retirement allowance under this chapter is pending, and a determination made in contravention of this sentence is of no effect. No period stated in subdivision 2 or in this subdivision, whether it is a period within which the Board is required to act or a period within which a determination is required to take effect, runs while such an application is pending or while a request the filing of which tolls the running of the member's final qualifying retirement date under subsection M is pending, except that the aggregate of all such non-running by reason of such requests and by reason of applications for a disability retirement allowance filed after the first such application shall not exceed 120 days, and a failure of the Board to act upon such a request within the period ~~allowed to it~~ **allowed by this section** for acting upon the request shall not extend that aggregate. For the purposes of this subdivision an application for a disability retirement allowance is pending from the date on which the member files it until the date on which the Board first acts upon it, and such a request is pending from the date on which the member files it until the date on which the Board first acts upon it.
M1: <u>**M. 1.** The Board shall adopt and publish, no later than July 1, 2029, procedures for administering this section, which shall address the content of a complete application, the channels through which an application may be filed, the determination of initial average compensation where records are incomplete, the determination and reservation of certified subsidies and contingency amounts, the waiting list, recertification, the crediting of service, settlement, cancellation, refunds, and the review of the Board's determinations. The Board shall publish the procedures on its website and shall make them available to any person on request.</u>
M2: <u>2. A member, retiree, beneficiary, applicant, personal representative of a deceased member's estate, person who has claimed any benefit payable on the death of a member, person to whom this section requires a notice to be given in respect of a benefit payable on the death of a member, or state agency from whose appropriation an amount was paid on a member's behalf, adversely affected by a determination of the Board under this section, or by a failure of the Board to make a determination, to give a notice, or to make a payment within a period required by this section, or by a failure of the Board to state in a certification or notice a matter this section requires to be stated in it, may obtain, upon written request filed within 30 days after the notice of the determination is given or, in the case of a failure to make a determination, to give a notice, or to make a payment, at any time before the Board makes the determination, gives the notice, or makes the payment or, where the Board has made the determination, given the notice, or made the payment late, within 30 days after the notice of the determination is given or, in the case of a failure to give a notice or to make a payment, within 30 days after the Board gives the notice or makes the payment, or, where the Board has made the determination late and has not given the notice of it that this section requires, at any time before it gives that notice, or, in the case of a failure to state a matter, within 30 days after the certification or notice is given or, where the provision that requires the matter to be stated provides a longer or later period, within that period, written reconsideration by the Board stating the reasons for its decision. Every determination, certification, redetermination, recertification, reduction, cancellation, rescission, restoration, crediting of service credit, placement on a waiting list, expiration of a reservation, denial of an election, and refusal to accept an election under this section is a determination of the Board for the purposes of this subsection, whether or not another provision of this section expressly provides for review of it. The Board shall act upon a request for reconsideration within 90 days **after the request is filed**. Where the Board does not act upon a request for reconsideration within ~~the 90 days allowed by this subsection~~ **the period allowed by this section for acting upon the request**, the person who filed the request may file with the Board written notice that the period has expired. Where the Board does not act upon the request within 30 days after that notice is filed, the request is denied on the first day after the expiration of those 30 days, and that denial constitutes the final determination of the Board upon the reconsideration and a case decision as defined in § 2.2-4001 for the purposes of this subsection. **Where a request is denied by operation of the preceding sentence, or where the Board does not act upon a request under the definition of "final qualifying retirement date" in subsection A within the period allowed by this section for acting upon it, the Board is deemed, for the purposes of every provision of this section and of subdivision B 4 f of § 51.1-142.2 under which a period begins or ends upon, or is measured from, the Board's acting, or last acting, upon the request, or under which a date is fixed by reference to the month in which the Board acts, or last acts, upon the request, to act upon the request, and to last act upon it, on the date of that denial or, as the case may be, on the day after the expiration of that period. Except for the purposes of the duty of the Board under this subsection to act upon an application no later than 15 days after it acts upon the request and the duty of the Board under the definition of "final qualifying retirement date" in subsection A to give a notice of a date required by that definition by reason of the Board's action upon a request, nothing in the preceding sentence determines the date by which the Board is required to act upon a request, to make a determination, or to give a notice or a decision, or whether the Board has performed such a duty within a period required by this section. The Board is not deemed by this subsection to have stated a member's final qualifying retirement date in a decision upon a request. The provision of this subsection deeming the Board to act upon a request applies where the Board does not act upon the request, and neither limits nor is limited by any provision of this section deeming the Board to act upon a request, and to last act upon it, on the date on which the Board first acts upon it, which applies where the Board acts upon a request more than once; the two provisions apply cumulatively, and neither is the exclusive rule for determining the date on which the Board acts upon a request.** The filing of a request for reconsideration under this subsection, and the filing of a request under the definition of "final qualifying retirement date" in subsection A, tolls the running of the member's final qualifying retirement date and of any period within which the member or applicant must act under this section or under subdivision B 4 f of § 51.1-142.2, until 30 days after the Board **gives written notice of its decision upon the request to the member and to the person who filed the request, but in no case earlier than 30 days after the Board** acts upon the request **and in no case later than 48 days after the Board acts upon the request**, except that (i) no second or subsequent request for reconsideration of the same determination or of the same failure, and no second or subsequent request under that definition, tolls any period under this section or under subdivision B 4 f of § 51.1-142.2, and (ii) the aggregate of all tolling under this subsection shall not exceed 120 days, excluding any period after the expiration of ~~the 90 days allowed by this subsection~~ **the period allowed by this section for acting upon the request** and before the Board acts upon the request, provided that the aggregate of all periods so excluded shall not exceed 90 days. An application that is the subject of a request for reconsideration under this subsection retains its filing date for the purposes of subdivisions D 4 and D 5 until ***120 days after*** the Board acts upon the request, and the Board shall act upon the application no later than 15 days after it acts upon the request. Upon completion of a reconsideration under this subsection, the final determination issued by the Board shall constitute a case decision as defined in § 2.2-4001. A member, retiree, beneficiary, applicant, personal representative of a deceased member's estate, person who has claimed any benefit payable on the death of a member, person to whom this section requires a notice to be given in respect of a benefit payable on the death of a member, or state agency from whose appropriation an amount was paid on a member's behalf, aggrieved by, and claiming the unlawfulness of, such case decision, shall have a right to seek judicial review thereof in accordance with Article 5 (§ 2.2-4025 et seq.) of the Administrative Process Act. Nothing in this subsection limits the right of any person under § 2.2-4026 to seek judicial review of a case decision. Articles 3 (§ 2.2-4018 et seq.) and 4 (§ 2.2-4024) of the Administrative Process Act shall not apply to a reconsideration under this subsection.</u>
M3: <u>3. The sentence of subsection B of § 2.2-4021 providing that a decision shall be deemed to be in favor of the named party, and the corresponding sentence of subsection C of that section, shall not apply to a determination of the Board under this section or to a reconsideration under subdivision 2.</u>
TITLE: **A BILL to amend and reenact §§ 51.1-142.2 and 51.1-162 of the Code of Virginia and to amend the Code of Virginia by adding a section numbered 51.1-142.4, relating to the Virginia Retirement System; purchase of prior active duty military service credit by state employees; cost; pilot program; death benefits; designation of beneficiary; reports.**
ENACT: **Be it enacted by the General Assembly of Virginia:**
